newsitem.title: USA: L.A. gang members convicted of murdering 3-year-old.
newsitem.headline: L.A. gang members convicted of murdering 3-year-old.

text.p: A jury on Monday found three presumed gang members guilty of murdering a 3-year-old girl who was in a car that made a wrong turn onto the gang's turf and died in a hail of bullets.

The jury was deadlocked on charges against a fourth alleged gang member and Los Angeles Superior Court Judge Edward Ferns set a July 1 hearing to determine whether the prosecution will seek to retry him.
The verdicts came after six days of deliberation in the so-called "wrong turn" murder of Stephanie Kuhen, who was hit in the head when the car in which she was riding was fired on.
The case attracted the attention of President Bill Clinton who used it early in his 1996 re-election campaign as an example of the need for a crackdown on violent street crimes.

The car, carrying six people, took a wrong turn returning from a birthday party in the early hours of Sept. 17, 1995. Gunfire also hit the driver, Timothy Stone, in the back and Stephanie's 2-year-old brother, Joey, in the foot.

The driver had mistakenly turned down a dead-end street dubbed "Street of Assassins" by the predominantly Hispanic gang that controlled the area. When he realised his mistake and tried to turn around, his car was met with a fusilade of gunfire.

During the trial, prosecutors said the motive for the shooting was that gang members believed Stone had "disrespected" them for driving onto their turf. Defence laywers urged the jury not to be swayed by emotion because of the defendants' gang affiliations and not to trust the evidence of a former gang member who was granted immunity.

The three convicted of murdering Stephanie and the attempted murder of the five other people in the car were: Anthony Rodriguez, 27, Manuel Rosales, 22, and Hugo David Gomez, 17. They all face maximum sentences of life in prison.
The jury could not reach a verdict for the fourth defendant, Augustin Lizama, 17.
